desc:
Daily order management starter sprint: a fixed, short period in which Ecom Swift LLC works through your orders each business day. We check new orders, flag problems, follow fulfilment, answer customer questions and send you a note at the end of every day.

## What is a daily order management sprint?

A daily order management sprint is a fixed run of business days in which someone else follows your store's order flow and reports back. It is a trial of outsourced order care, so you can judge the quality and the fit before choosing anything longer.

Each day follows the same routine we agree with you at the start. The scope is bounded by the package, which keeps the cost and the commitment clear.

## Why orders need daily attention

An order is not finished when the customer pays. It can stall at many points: a failed address check, a stock mismatch, a payment held for review, a parcel with no tracking, a customer who writes in a panic. Left alone for a day or two, small issues turn into late deliveries and refund requests.

Founders often know this and still cannot watch the queue, because they are building products, handling suppliers or running marketing. A short daily routine catches trouble while it is still cheap to fix.

## How daily care affects customers and cash flow

Quick follow-up improves the thing customers care about most: whether the parcel arrives when promised. When a stuck order is spotted on the day it stalls, you can contact the shopper before they notice, and many complaints never happen.

It also protects revenue. Orders that sit unfulfilled risk cancellations and disputes, and paid orders that never reach the warehouse are money tied up. A daily check keeps the pipeline moving and shows you where delays repeat.

## What a good daily routine includes

- A morning check of every new order for address, stock and payment status.
- A list of problem orders with a suggested next step for each.
- Follow-up on fulfilment, so paid orders reach the warehouse or partner.
- Tracking checks, with a note on parcels that stop moving.
- Answers to customer order emails, in your voice and policy.
- Handling of returns, where the package covers them.
- A short end-of-day note listing what was done and what is open.
- A weekly summary of orders, issues and delays.
- A closing review with advice on what to change.

## What we do

On day one we agree the routine with you: which orders to check, what we may decide alone and what must wait for your approval. We use the access you give us as a staff or collaborator user, with limited permissions. We do not touch your payment settings or products unless you ask.

Each business day we run the routine, record what we found and send the note. If something needs a quick decision, we message you with a clear question and a suggested answer. At the end of the sprint, we review what worked and what you might automate, outsource or change.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the length of the sprint and in how much we handle, from order checks only to customer emails, returns and a review call. Continuing monthly care is quoted separately, so there is no hidden renewal.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us your cut-off times and shipping promises.
- Name the orders or customers that need special care.
- Reply to our open questions each day, even briefly.
- Share your usual fixes for common issues.

**Avoid:**
- Giving us full admin rights when limited staff access will do.
- Keeping rules in your head instead of writing them down.
- Changing the routine halfway without telling us.
- Judging the sprint on a single odd order.

## Who this is for

This fits a store owner who is stretched thin around a launch or a seasonal peak. It suits a business that is deciding whether to hire a part-time order assistant. It also suits a store recovering from a messy week that needs someone to tidy the queue and restore order.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of your fulfilment path, your policies and the apps you use. Add us as a collaborator, staff or team user, with permission to view and manage orders. We never request passwords. After you order, we send a checklist and a proposed routine, and we start when you approve it.
